title: [D8 Guardrails] Conformance suite for 'behaviour that must be impossible'
summary: `concept/07-principles.md`'s twenty-row must-never-happen table is now an executable suite: `tests/test_conformance.py` holds one named test per row (`MNH-01`..`MNH-20`, the note's own order), each executing the row's property against real objects, a real capture or the real engine. Four meta-tests parse the note on every run so that adding, removing or rewording a row is red until a test carries it, and a `conformance` marker plus `make conformance` make the gate runnable on its own.
assumption_validated: That the table can be made executable end to end rather than partly — that every row has a seam where the guarantee can be run, not merely read. It can: all twenty execute, and the suite found no violation of any row in the tree as it stands. What this increment also establishes, and did not assume, is that the gate itself has to be tested: the three ways it rots (a row added, a conformance test renamed, a row's in-depth coverage deleted) were each induced by a temporary mutation and each turned the suite red, then reverted. A gate that is only asserted to work is exactly the failure mode `concept/07` is about.
makes_buildable: Task 50 (architectural boundary tests) gets the pattern and the two AST helpers it will want: `_names(path)` and `_statements(path)` read a module's identifiers and its non-docstring string literals, which is what makes 'this module holds no HTTP client' checkable without a text search finding the comment arguing for the thing's absence. `MAY_HOLD_A_CREDENTIAL` is the shape a 'which module may reach what' assertion takes here. Task 51 (secrets hygiene) inherits MNH-15 as the frame to deepen: the prompt and the disclosure-record channels are covered against a real `Settings`, and the repository channel is explicitly deferred to it and named in the test's own docstring, so 51 extends a test rather than inventing where the row lives. Task 52 (end to end) gets MNH-20 as the enforcement for the acceptance definition it writes: the disclaimers in README.md and docs/overview-slides.md are now load-bearing text that the suite requires to be present, so a claim growing past 'the stages compose and cite' is caught. Task 55 (deferred register and open questions) gets `COVERED_BY` as a live index from a concept row to the tests that hold it.

verification.detail: 1781 passed, 1 skipped in 794 s. The new module is 27 tests (20 rows, two of them parametrized into two cases, plus four meta-tests over the table itself); `uv run pytest -q tests/test_conformance.py` is 27 passed in 30 s and `make conformance` is 27 passed, 1755 deselected. Seven of the twenty run against the engine: MNH-01 loads the real ThreatFox extract through the real loader over the committed capture and reads `helena_analytical_enriched_context`; MNH-06 renders a real context at the tightest budget that renders at all; MNH-11, MNH-12 and MNH-18 query `information_schema` on the migrated schema; MNH-16 executes `rendering.ENRICHMENT_QUERY` against a stand-in relation on a throwaway schema. The gate was proved to bite rather than assumed to: appending a row to `concept/07-principles.md` turned two meta-tests red, renaming `test_mnh13_*` turned one red, breaking one `COVERED_BY` reference turned one red, and adding 'The verdicts are right.' and 'Inference is run locally on this machine.' to README.md turned MNH-20 and MNH-19 red. Every mutation was reverted and `git status` confirmed clean. `uv lock --check` and `python -m compileall src tests scripts` both pass. The pre-change baseline was 1754 passed, 1 skipped in 734 s.

invariant_conflicts.detail: `concept/07-principles.md:187` says **"Local pipeline" means local inference and decisions, not zero network egress.** That contradicts two things: its own disclosure table eight lines above, which says model inference is *"Hosted, not on-premises"*; and `concept/03-architecture.md:204`, which says **"Local" means decisions and control stay local** and then **"No document may describe the pipeline as running models locally while it does not."** 07:187 appears to have `inference` where 03 has `control`. Nothing was changed: `concept/` is the authority and `instruction.md` says a note-level disagreement is a defect to report rather than to pick a side of. The practical consequence is recorded in the test: `test_mnh19_*` scans README.md, docs/ and src/helena/ and deliberately does NOT scan `concept/`, because a conformance test that could fail on the authoritative source is a test that invites editing the authority to go green. If 07:187 is corrected to say 'decisions and control', nothing here needs to change.

invariant_conflicts.kind: task steps are narrower than the concept
invariant_conflicts.detail: The task's steps enumerate eighteen rows, stopping at 'a cited context evicted rather than frozen'. The note's table has twenty: it also holds 'The pipeline is described as running models locally' and '"The prototype works" is read as "the verdicts are right"'. `concept/` outranks `prd.json`, and the step that matters says *one named test per row*, so both were written (MNH-19, MNH-20). They are prose-conformance tests over what this repository says about itself, which is what those two rows are about — they are the only two rows whose subject is a claim rather than a code path.

deferred: MNH-15's repository channel — a scan of committed files for live credential values. The row names five channels; the log, the URL and the exception are `tests/test_observability.py`'s against the real key, the agent-visible tool surface is `tests/test_tools.py`'s against the real key, and this increment added the two that had no owner (the prompt bytes, and the disclosure record of having sent them) against a controlled `Settings`. The repository scan is task 51's, which owns secrets hygiene and the key-in-URL exposure profile in full; MNH-15's docstring says so by name, so 51 extends this test rather than deciding where the row lives.

MNH-16 against a real analyst-tier row. The tier filter is executed — `rendering.ENRICHMENT_QUERY` really runs — but against a stand-in relation of the same name and shape, because nothing in this repository writes an `analyst`-tier row into `helena_analytical_enriched_context`: the tier is a literal in `sql/migrations/0014_feed_mapping_views.sql`. `tests/test_rendering.py` made the same choice for the same reason and the limitation is unchanged by this increment; it closes when something joins the analyst cache into the enriched view.

A row-level mutation test for each of the twenty. The three meta-gate failure modes were induced and verified, and two of the prose rows were induced and verified, but the other eighteen rows' tests were not individually proved to fail against a deliberately broken implementation — that would mean mutating src/ eighteen times. What is claimed is that they execute and pass, not that each has been shown to catch its own violation.
lessons: A conformance suite over a document has to read the document at run time, not copy it. `ROWS` holds each row verbatim and `_table()` re-parses `concept/07-principles.md` on every run, so a reworded row is red rather than silently leaving a test asserting a sentence nobody wrote any more. Copying the table into the test file once would have produced a gate that passes while checking the wrong thing.

Naming a row's in-depth coverage and RESOLVING the names is worth more than duplicating it. `COVERED_BY` maps each row to the `module::test` entries that hold it in depth, and a meta-test parses those files' ASTs to check every name still exists. That turns 'someone deleted the only test for this guarantee' into a failure at the row, and it cost about sixty lines instead of a second copy of the fifteen-case composition table.

Read source with `ast`, not with `re`, when the question is 'does this module do X'. Three checks in this module were written as text searches first and all three were wrong in the same way: `src/helena/agents.py` quotes `concept/07`'s 'Secrets and configuration' heading, so `\bSecret\b` matched prose; `src/helena/context.py`'s own docstring says 'retention is a filter, not a delete', so a search for DELETE found the sentence arguing for the thing's absence. `_names()` (identifiers referenced as code) and `_statements()` (string literals that are not docstrings) are the two helpers that fixed it, and they are the same lesson `prds/CONTEXT.md` already records about asserting on SQL text.

Hard-wrapped Markdown defeats substring matching. The sentences MNH-19 and MNH-20 require to be present span a newline in README.md, so `sentence in path.read_text()` failed on the wrapping rather than on the claim. `_prose()` collapses whitespace before matching.

A disclaimer contains the claim it disclaims. MNH-20's first version flagged `docs/overview-slides.md`'s own 'Nothing here claims the verdicts are right.' A forbidden-claim regex over prose needs a negation guard on the text preceding the match, or it fails on exactly the sentence it exists to require.

The three failure modes of a gate are worth inducing before trusting it. Appending a row to the note, renaming a conformance test, and breaking a `COVERED_BY` reference were each done to the working tree, run, observed red, and reverted. Two of them would have passed silently under the first implementation: `test_every_row_of_the_table_has_a_test_named_for_it` originally iterated `ROWS` rather than the note, so a row added to `concept/` was caught only after someone had already copied it into the test file.
failed_approaches: task 49: `pgrep -f "pytest -q"` to tell whether a background suite run had finished. It matches the AGENT'S OWN PROCESS, because `implement.sh` passes the whole PRD task text as an argv element and this task's text contains the string `uv run pytest -q`. It reported RUNNING for several turns after the run had ended, and cost about ten minutes of polling. This is the same hazard `session-memory.json` records for task 03 with `bin/risingwave` and `single_node`, generalised: ANY `pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` pattern that appears in the task prompt matches the session itself. Use `pgrep -x pytest`, `pgrep -x risingwave`, `pgrep -x blink`, or read the background command's own output file.

task 49: Asserting MNH-01's `failed` and `missing` states in one store, one after the other. They are mutually exclusive by construction — an attempt that failed before the window is precisely what makes that window `failed` rather than `missing` — so the second assertion found no rows. The test is parametrized over the two states with a fresh `context` fixture each, which is also the more honest shape: the distinction between them is the row.

task 49: `pytest.raises(Exception)` for the six version registries in MNH-17. It passes for the right reason and would also pass for a `TypeError` from a changed signature, which is the break the row cares about. Each registry has its own `UnknownVersion` subclass, so the table carries the expected type per dimension and the test names it.

task 49: Running a second `pytest` while the full suite was in flight, to check the new module. Only one engine runs per machine (task 03), and although per-test schemas kept the two runs from corrupting each other, editing the module after a full run had already collected it meant that run validated a file that no longer existed. The full suite was stopped and re-run once against the final tree instead.
next_session_should_know: The must-never-happen table is executable and the gate is wired. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE ENTRY POINTS ARE `make conformance` (27 tests, ~30 s) AND THE `conformance` MARKER, registered in `pyproject.toml`. It is NOT a second suite — it is collected by `uv run pytest -q` and therefore by `make check`, which is what makes it required; the marker exists so 'do the guarantees still hold' can be asked on its own, exactly as `make acceptance` already works for the D3 gate. (2) ADDING A ROW TO `concept/07-principles.md`'s TABLE MEANS ADDING A TEST, AND THE SUITE ENFORCES IT. `tests/test_conformance.py` re-parses the note every run. A row with no `test_mnhNN_…` is red; a test naming a row the table does not hold is red; a reworded row whose text no longer matches `ROWS` is red. All three were induced and reverted, so this is measured rather than intended. The identifiers are positional: `MNH-01` is the first row of the table, `MNH-20` the last, and inserting a row in the middle renumbers everything after it — which is correct, and is why the identifier lives only in the test name and in `ROWS`, never in `src/`. (3) `COVERED_BY` IS A LIVE INDEX FROM A CONCEPT ROW TO THE TESTS THAT HOLD IT, and the names are resolved by AST on every run. If you rename a test that module names — there are 40 of them across 13 modules — the conformance suite fails at the row, not at your module. Carry the new name across; do not delete the entry, because an entry deleted is a row whose only deep coverage can then vanish unnoticed. (4) TWO AST HELPERS ARE THERE FOR TASK 50 TO REUSE: `_names(path)` returns every identifier a module references as code, and `_statements(path)` returns every string literal that is not a docstring. Both exist because the text-search versions were wrong — `agents.py` quotes `concept/07`'s 'Secrets and configuration' heading and `context.py`'s docstring says 'not a delete', so a regex finds the prose arguing for the thing's absence. `_prose(path)` collapses whitespace for the two prose rows, because the sentences they require span a hard wrap. (5) MNH-19 AND MNH-20 MAKE THE DISCLAIMERS LOAD-BEARING. `README.md`'s 'No claim is made here about verdict quality', `docs/overview-slides.md`'s 'the labelled evaluation corpus does not exist' and 'Nothing here claims the verdicts are right', and `src/helena/disclosure.py`'s 'Inference in the prototype is hosted' are now required to be present, and no committed file under `docs/`, the repository root or `src/helena/` may claim an accuracy figure or local inference. If task 52 rewrites the acceptance statement, keep those sentences or update the two tables at the top of those tests. `concept/` is deliberately not scanned — see the invariant conflict below, and do not 'fix' that by widening the glob. (6) THERE IS A REAL DEFECT IN `concept/07-principles.md:187`. It says '"Local pipeline" means local inference and decisions', which contradicts its own disclosure table ('Hosted, not on-premises') and `concept/03-architecture.md:204` ('"Local" means decisions and control stay local'). It looks like `inference` was written where `control` was meant. Nothing was edited — `concept/` is the authority — but it is why MNH-19 scans what the repository says about itself rather than its source. This is an operator decision, not a session's. (7) NEVER USE `pgrep -f` OR `pkill -f` FROM INSIDE A SESSION. The runner passes the whole task text as argv, so a pattern like `pytest -q` matches the agent's own process. Task 03 lost commands to SIGTERM this way; this session read a finished suite as still-running for several turns. `pgrep -x pytest` / `pgrep -x risingwave` / `pgrep -x blink`, or a pidfile.
